### Observed differences

- The order of a middle segment of activities is reversed. In the earlier window, A20, A22 and A23 sat at about 40% of the trace (medians 0.39–0.40) and A19, A21 and A24 at about 67–70%, with A25 (about 0.45) and A29 (about 0.66) between them; in the later window, A19, A21 and A24 sit at about 35–38% and A20, A22 and A23 at about 64–66%, with A25 (about 0.38) and A29 (about 0.59) still between the two groups. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009]
- Pairwise relations flip in the same direction: A20 preceded A25 in about 98–99 in 100 traces earlier, and A25 precedes A20 in about 97–98 in 100 later, while the two still co-occur in every trace; the same reversal holds for A20 with A29 and for A22 and A23 with A25 and A29. A19 moved from after A20, A22, A23, A25 and A29 (following them in about 31 in 100 shared traces) to before them (about 42 in 100), and A21 and A24 likewise swapped from running after A20, A22, A23, A25 and A29 to running before them. [REL015–REL035]
- Successors moved with the blocks: earlier, A19, A21 and A24 led almost exclusively to A30 (about 95–97 in 100 of their outgoing transitions) and A20, A22 and A23 led mainly to A25 (about 30–38 in 100); later, A19, A21 and A24 lead to A25 (about 97–98 in 100) and A20, A22 and A23 lead to A30 (about 31–33 in 100). A29 now feeds into A20, A22 and A23 (about 97 in 100) where it previously fed into A19, A21 and A24, and A40 switched the same way; typical distances changed accordingly (A29 to A30 usually two steps earlier versus four steps later; A40 to A25 four steps earlier versus two steps later). [DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012, LAG019, LAG025]
- A02 became a frequent early step between A14 and A15: it appears in about 65 in 100 later traces versus about 15 in 100 earlier, at an earlier position (mean about 0.20 versus 0.53). Earlier, A14 led directly to A15 (about 84 in 100 of A14's outgoing transitions); later, A14 leads to A02 (about 60 in 100, within one step in about 98 in 100 of the traces containing both) and A02 leads on to A15 (about 87 in 100 of A02's outgoing transitions). [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR004, LAG005, REL001, REL002]
- A06 and A10 are now rarely executed: about 5 in 100 traces for A06 (from about 21 in 100) and about 6 in 100 for A10 (from about 17 in 100). [OCC002, OCC003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, two groups of activities exchanged their place in the sequence: A19, A21 and A24, which previously ran after the middle activities A25 and A29 and after A20, A22 and A23, now run before them, while A20, A22 and A23 now run after A25 and A29. The signs are direct and consistent across indicator types: near-deterministic order reversals in pairs that still co-occur in essentially every trace (A20 before A25 in about 98–99 in 100 traces earlier versus A25 before A20 in about 97–98 in 100 later), opposite position shifts of the two groups (about 0.40 to 0.65 for A20/A22/A23 and about 0.68 to 0.37 for A19/A21/A24), and matching successor changes on both sides, including A29 and A40 now leading into the other group. Screening supports the overall picture: 87 control-flow items qualified against about 1 expected for an unchanged process, so chance sampling cannot account for the pattern as a whole. Limitations: positions are event positions rather than clock time, so nothing is claimed about calendar timing; the evidence cannot distinguish a reordering of a single flow from a shift in the mix of pre-existing variants; and the order within each group (among A19/A21/A24 and among A20/A22/A23) is not constrained by the observed pairs. [REL022, REL023, REL015, POS003, POS005, POS006, POS002, POS004, POS007, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012]

Other differences:
- A02 appears to have been inserted as a new step between A14 and A15: its participation rose from about 15% to about 65% of traces, A14 now leads to A02 (about 60 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, where it previously went directly to A15 in about 84 in 100), and A02 leads on to A15 (about 87 in 100). [OCC001, DIR001, DIR004, LAG005, REL001, REL002]
- A06 and A10 are executed far less often in the later window, in about 5 and 6 in 100 traces versus about 21 and 17 in 100 earlier. [OCC002, OCC003]

Now I need to figure out what the underlying behavioural difference is.

OCC001: A02 participation rose from 15% to 64.5% of traces; mean occurrences per trace 0.165 → 0.685. Support 30 → 129.

OCC002: A06 participation fell from 21.5% to 5%. Support 43 → 10.

OCC003: A10 participation fell from 16.5% to 6%. Support 33 → 12.
